issues.description: onTestRunStart silently swallows a null result from findChangedFiles and degrades to no filter
issues.detail: When vitestGit.findChangedFiles returns null (e.g., not a git repository, ref does not exist), `this.changedFiles = changedFiles ?? undefined` quietly disables the filter and coverage reports everything. The postcondition the user requested is 'coverage limited to changed files'; the implemented postcondition is 'limited if git cooperates, otherwise unrestricted'. This is a TESTED-NOT-PROVED failure mode: no test exercises the null branch. Refuse silent fallback; warn or fail.

issues.description: isIncluded mutates globCache with results that depend on changedFiles state, violating cache invariant
issues.detail: The cache key is `filename` alone, but the value now depends on (filename, changedFiles). onTestRunStart clears the cache, but any caller that invokes isIncluded before onTestRunStart fires (or in a re-run where changedFiles is reassigned) poisons the cache. State the invariant: cache value is a pure function of key. The current code violates it. Either include changedFiles in the key or assert ordering.

issues.description: changedFiles comparison uses string identity on paths of unspecified normalization
issues.detail: `this.changedFiles.includes(filename)` after `slash(cleanUrl(_filename))` assumes findChangedFiles returns paths in the identical normalized form (forward slashes, no query string, same absolute/relative basis as the filename passed to isIncluded). No precondition is stated or enforced anywhere. On Windows or with relative-vs-absolute mismatches this silently filters everything out. State the path-form invariant and assert it.

issues.description: onTestRunStart hook ordering is duplicated across three call sites with no documented invariant
issues.detail: core.ts now calls `coverageProvider?.onTestRunStart?.()` after `_testRun.start(...)` in three places. The precondition 'onTestRunStart runs exactly once per test run, after start, before file reporting' is enforced by convention only. A fourth code path will forget. Extract one helper or document the invariant on the interface; otherwise the next contributor smuggles a fourth call site and the invariant rots.

issues.description: CLI transform accepts boolean inputs that the declared argument type cannot produce
issues.detail: The transform checks `value === true || value === false`, but the CLI argument is declared `<commit/branch>`, which yields strings. The dead branches suggest the author was unsure of the precondition on `value`. State it: from the CLI, `value: string`; from programmatic config, the resolver path is different. Remove the impossible branches or document why they are reachable.

issues.description: Inheritance condition `=== undefined` is fragile against explicit `false`
issues.detail: `if (resolved.coverage.changed === undefined && resolved.changed !== undefined)` works only because the default is left unset rather than defaulted to `false`. The docs say default is `false`. If a future defaulting pass fills in `false`, inheritance silently breaks and the public.test contract is the only thing that catches it. State whether the default is 'unset' or 'false' and pick one.

review.summary: The feature is straightforward in intent but the implementation has not been reasoned about end-to-end. Two correctness invariants are unstated and violated: the globCache is no longer a pure function of its key, and the equality check between `changedFiles` entries and the normalized filename assumes a path form that is nowhere asserted. A null return from `findChangedFiles` silently degrades the postcondition the user asked for. The control flow is structured, but the onTestRunStart hook is invoked at three sites with the ordering invariant carried only by convention — a smuggled coupling. TESTED-NOT-PROVED on the failure paths; REASONED on the happy path only.
